renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Whatever strange things happen in you while this works, do not be afraid of any of them — the Goddess is playing. She is drunk on sweet nectar and makes many changes, using up what you did in many past lives.

She shakes the stained parts of you free from their trap, lifted by the highest power. That is reaching the stage. When the change passes through, your hair stands up, tears fall, you yawn, your voice shakes, knots burst, and drops throb up from deep in the belly.

That is the final stage. Next comes rest: when she wakes and pours out from the belly wheel, all your senses shut down and stand outside. She melts into the highest place. The knower finds nothing else to know — she rests in God, and that is rest.

Where she rests, send your mind to melt away too. Then the self is known as one with the highest, by those who hold firm. You become God yourself — that is the change. And you rain sweet nectar forever, the food of all living things. Hold your mind there, and she comes back in. That is the return — thirteen in full, nothing more.

renders.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms.

paragraphs.text: Whatever weird stuff your system does during this — zero fear. She is playing. Nectar-drunk, she remixes everything, burning through karma from lives ago.
She shakes the stained bits loose from the trap, running on supreme power. Stage reached. Full-body signals: hair up, tears, yawns, shaky voice, knots popping, drops throbbing from the gut.

That is the final stage, logged. Now rest: she wakes and pours from the belly wheel, senses shut down and stand outside, she dissolves into the top floor. Knower finds nothing else. She rests in God. Rest: defined.

Park your mind where she rests and let it dissolve. The self reads as supreme — firm ones only. You turn God. That is the transformation. Then you rain sweet nectar nonstop, food for everything alive. Mind held, she re-enters. Return: complete. Thirteen of thirteen.
